title: New product from PRD: one form in the browser reaches a bound repository and a goal
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0, the scaffold) and child 2 (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, the command). PROOF ROW: it owns the browser form, the Playwright journey, the live GitHub drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the 'New product from PRD' form in the browser - directory (new or empty), PRD file, product name, optional GitHub owner/visibility - dispatching child 2's command and then creating the goal with the PRD through the EXISTING `goal.create_with_source`, after which the existing lane continues unchanged.

THE WHOLE POINT IS THAT THE BROWSER IS ENOUGH. This is the row that makes 'a fresh project cannot be started from the browser alone' false - a README clause measured true on 2026-09-03. The journey must therefore use NO scratchpad script and NO seed for any step the product claims to do itself; a bootstrap driven by a helper script proves nothing about the browser.

REFUSALS ARE OPERATOR WORDS. All four of child 2's codes surface here, and BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE is the interesting one: the local bootstrap SUCCEEDED and the GitHub half did not, so the form must say exactly that rather than reading as a total failure. An operator told 'bootstrap failed' when they have a perfectly good local repository will delete it and start again.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): goal creation from a PRD already exists (`goal.create_with_source`), and the existing goal-create surface is at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts (its :91 sentence, 'cannot drive the pre-activation chain', is the kind of honest blocker wording this form should reuse rather than invent). The Playwright specs under tests/e2e/control-room/ already drive a real daemon.
definitionOfDone: A 'New product from PRD' form takes directory, PRD file, product name and OPTIONAL GitHub owner/visibility, and dispatches child 2's command. The GitHub fields are visibly optional - a form that implies GitHub is required would hide the local-only path that child 2 exists to support.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon completes the whole thing from the browser: directory created, first commit exists (`git log --oneline` = exactly 1 line), repository bound, project in the manager catalog, PRD goal created and the lane continuing. `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. NO scratchpad script and NO seed is used for any step - this row's claim is that the BROWSER is sufficient, and a helper script anywhere in the path voids it.

The four refusals render as operator words with their codes VERBATIM, and BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE renders as a PARTIAL success: the local repository exists and is bound, only the GitHub half did not. Assert that wording specifically - 'bootstrap failed' here would make an operator delete a good repository.

LIVE DRIVE: a throwaway repository created under the owner's GitHub account from the browser - URL and receipt id in a row comment under ~4500 chars. The owner's account and visibility are supplied by the owner, never invented. If `gh` is absent or unauthenticated on the lane, record the BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE refusal verbatim together with the successful LOCAL bootstrap - that is a complete outcome, not a partial one.

README's 'a fresh project cannot be started from the browser alone' clause and the VISION Stage 2 'repository bootstrapping' / 'new repository creation' status lines are rewritten to the measured truth, WITH the date of the live drive. `git grep -n 'cannot be started from the browser alone'` returns 0 hits.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NO SCRIPT, NO SEED, ANYWHERE IN THE JOURNEY. The claim is that the browser alone is sufficient; a scratchpad helper in the path makes the claim false while the test stays green.
A PARTIAL SUCCESS IS RENDERED AS ONE. BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE means the local repository is fine - say so, or an operator destroys good work.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: a scaffold defect is child 1's, a command defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
THE OWNER'S GITHUB ACCOUNT AND VISIBILITY ARE THE OWNER'S. Never invent an owner, never make a repository public by default, and never let a credential reach the form or a log.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
THE FORM (DoD 1). Add the "New product from PRD" surface as a NEW component under apps/control-room/src/v2/ — do not grow live-goal-create.ts, which is already 229 lines against a 250-line target.

FIELDS: directory (new or empty), PRD file, product name, and GitHub owner + visibility marked VISIBLY OPTIONAL. A form that implies GitHub is required hides the local-only path child 2 exists to support, and that is the single most likely way this row ships something worse than nothing.

VISIBILITY HAS NO DEFAULT THAT CREATES A PUBLIC REPOSITORY. The owner supplies owner and visibility; never invent an owner, never preselect public. No credential field, ever — `gh` uses the operator's own CLI auth (child 2's rail), so a token has no reason to reach this form, a log line, or a receipt.

COPY PATTERN: reuse the shape at live-goal-create.ts:90-100 — a refusal names the specific reason AND a next step that names a card on THIS screen; prerequisites come from the production label helper, never a paraphrase. Do not reuse the sentence the description quotes; it was deleted.

CONSTRAINTS from the row rails: ASCII-only sources, apostrophe-free JSX text (the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX), and check the new testid namespace is FREE before claiming it — `git grep -n "cr\.<namespace>" -- apps tests` — because `cr.board.*` was already taken once.

DISPATCH AND COMPOSITION. Wire the form to child 2's command, then to the EXISTING goal creation.

1. Add the `repository.bootstrap` payload to the dispatch table in apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts (285 lines; `DEV_PAYLOADS` at :56 with `project.bind_repository` at :117, `PLANNING_CHAIN_STEPS` at :166). FIRST determine which table the V2 PRODUCT surface actually reads — `DEV_PAYLOADS` is the legacy dev board's, and `main.tsx:101` serves the legacy shell only for `?v1=1`. Adding to the wrong table wires a surface no operator sees.
2. After the command succeeds, create the goal with the PRD through the EXISTING `goal.create_with_source`. Do NOT write a second goal-creation path; the existing lane continues unchanged after this point, and that is the whole design.
3. The payload carries directory, product name, profile version and the OPTIONAL owner/visibility. It carries no credential.

MOUNT THE FORM where an operator can reach it without a URL parameter, and add the route/nav entry in the same step — a component no screen renders is dead code that satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

If the payload shape child 2 published differs from what you expect, use CHILD 2's shape and say so. A second shape that happens to typecheck is a contract drift the epic-final row will find.

THE FOUR REFUSALS AS OPERATOR WORDS (DoD 3) — component test, `new-product-form.test.tsx`.

All four of child 2's codes render with their code VERBATIM plus operator words. Assert the RENDERED TEXT by exact match, not a substring that a reworded sentence would still satisfy.

BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND IT GETS ITS OWN ARM. It is a PARTIAL SUCCESS: the local repository exists, is committed and is bound; only the GitHub half did not happen. The copy must say that. An operator told "bootstrap failed" when they hold a perfectly good local repository will delete it and start again — that is the concrete harm, and it is why this arm asserts the wording specifically rather than asserting that some error appeared. Assert the copy does NOT contain a total-failure word, and DOES name the local repository as intact.

MUTATE AND CONFIRM RED: change the partial-success copy to a generic failure string and confirm the arm reds. A refusal-rendering test that has never been seen red is not evidence.

Also assert: no rendered string contains a token-shaped value on any path (epic rail 3), and the GitHub fields read as optional in the rendered output, not merely in a comment.

THE JOURNEY (DoD 2) — a NEW spec, tests/e2e/control-room/new-product-from-prd.spec.ts. Do NOT edit tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts: it is a peer's untracked in-flight file owned by task-ac9d5e2d, and editing it in the shared checkout is a collision. REUSE its harness and its lessons.

HARNESS: `withDaemonBackedControlRoom` / `DaemonLane` from ./daemon-ports.js, `seed: "NONE"`. Assert `lane.seedPid` is NULL before touching the page — documented at daemon-ports.ts:245-249, worked example at board-chain.spec.ts:429-434. A journey that cannot prove it ran unseeded proves nothing here.

NO SCRIPT AND NO SEED ANYWHERE IN THE PATH (row rail 1). The claim is that the BROWSER is sufficient; a scratchpad helper anywhere makes the claim false while the test stays green. Assert the absence structurally, not by intention.

THREE LESSONS CARRIED FROM THE PEER SPEC, each already paid for:
- Drive the bare `lane.baseUrl`. `main.tsx:101` serves the legacy shell only for `?v1=1`, so a journey clicking `cr.liveboard.*` re-proves the old dev board and leaves the shipped surface untested.
- SEAT THE RECORDER BEFORE THE FIRST CLICK — a card's dispatch report lives only until the next surface poll re-keys the card (board-chain.spec.ts:26-33), so a watcher on its own schedule can watch a dispatch succeed and see nothing.
- Assert receipts as MEASURED: read the lane's HEAD sha from GIT, never from what the page said, and fail a row that reads as a `<projectId>-*` literal — that shape is what a placeholder looks like.

ASSERT THE WHOLE OUTCOME: directory created; `git log --oneline` in it is EXACTLY ONE line (assert the line count, not a substring); repository bound; project in the manager catalog; the PRD goal created; the lane continuing. Quote the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line.

TEARDOWN: the lane, the daemon child and the created directory released in a `finally`, on the throwing path too (epic rail 4) — a leaked port or directory makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

THE LOCAL-ONLY VARIANT — same spec, its own arm, and the one that guards the row's most important behaviour.

Run the journey with the GitHub fields LEFT EMPTY. Assert it SUCCEEDS end to end: directory, single commit, bound repository, catalog entry, goal created — with no GitHub interaction attempted at all. A local-only bootstrap is a success, not a degraded mode.

Then run it with GitHub requested but `gh` unavailable on the lane. Assert the form renders the PARTIAL-SUCCESS copy from step 4, and assert the LOCAL half still completed: the repository exists, is committed and is bound. This is the arm that stops a future change from turning a missing `gh` into a total failure.

ASSERT BOTH VARIANTS ACTUALLY RAN. If they share a table or a loop, assert the case count — a swept case that silently yields zero cases passes. Two variants that produce identical end states would mean the GitHub half changed nothing, which is a finding rather than a pass.

THE LIVE DRIVE (DoD 4). Create a THROWAWAY repository under the OWNER'S GitHub account, from the browser, and record the URL and receipt id in a row comment under ~4500 chars (comments truncate silently at 5000).

THE OWNER SUPPLIES THE ACCOUNT AND THE VISIBILITY. Never invent an owner. Never make a repository public by default. If the owner has not supplied them, ASK in the row comment and take the `gh`-absent outcome below rather than guessing — a public repository created under someone's account without their say is not undoable by deleting it.

IF `gh` IS ABSENT OR UNAUTHENTICATED ON THE LANE, that is a COMPLETE outcome, not a partial one: record the `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` refusal VERBATIM together with the successful LOCAL bootstrap — directory, single commit, bound repository, catalog entry. Do not treat it as a failed step and do not retry with a different account.

NO CREDENTIAL IN THE COMMENT, the transcript, or a screenshot. Check the transcript before pasting: `gh` output can echo a remote URL with embedded userinfo (epic rail 3).

Record the date of the drive — step 8's doc edit is dated to it.

THE DOCS (DoD 5) — AND THE GATE AS WRITTEN IS ALREADY VACUOUS, so read this before editing.

MEASURED: `git grep -n "cannot be started from the browser alone"` returns ZERO HITS at HEAD. task-ac9d5e2d already removed that sentence. Running the DoD's grep and reporting 0 proves NOTHING about this row's work — report it as already-satisfied-on-arrival, name the row that satisfied it, and do the real work below. Do not claim credit for a gate that was green before you started.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is a DIFFERENT claim: README:29 now reads "**Fresh start, from the browser alone**: the Activate project card reads the..." — that is about ACTIVATING AN EXISTING project. This row shipped something else: CREATING A NEW PRODUCT REPOSITORY from a PRD. Add or correct the sentence that covers the new capability, dated to step 7's live drive, and make sure the two claims are distinguishable to a reader — conflating them would overstate what ships.

VISION: docs/VISION.md:141 ("**Stage 2 - PRD to deployed MVP:** repository bootstrapping; ...") and :127 ("Support exceptionally well: new repository creation; ...") are the status lines. Rewrite to the MEASURED truth with the live-drive date — and only for repository bootstrapping. The other Stage 2 items (infrastructure generation, deployment, secrets, migrations, monitoring) are other rows' and must not be marked shipped here.

Do NOT re-edit the README and runbook sentences task-ac9d5e2d rewrote. If you believe one is now wrong, comment on that row.

If a doc needed no change, name the files you READ to reach that conclusion.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 6).

GATES — each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser`
Name explicitly that root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so the control-room leg carries the apps/** claim. Path-attributed baseline: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths; complete only when that intersection is EMPTY, and disclose foreign red verbatim with its failing paths.

ADVERSARIAL PASS, as an attacker on an operator-supplied form:
- What does the form do with a directory that is NOT empty? The refusal must be BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY rendered as operator words, and NOTHING may be written — this is the path where a wrong directory buries someone's work.
- A directory path that escapes, a UNC path, an empty string, a path that is a FILE. Each needs a defined answer.
- A product name with a quote, a slash, a leading dot, or 200 characters — child 1 validates it, so assert the refusal SURFACES rather than crashing the form.
- A PRD file that is enormous, empty, or not text.
- DOUBLE SUBMIT: two clicks in flight at once. Does the second refuse DIR_NOT_EMPTY, or does it race the first into a half-written tree? Assert which.
- Does any error path, log line or screenshot carry a credential or a remote URL with embedded userinfo?
- ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX confirmed by the scheduler boundary scan; every production file under 250 lines (`wc -l` the new files and quote it).

A DEFECT FOUND HERE IS NOT FIXED HERE (row rail 3): a scaffold defect is child 1's (task-4a0f7064), a command defect is child 2's (task-facff1d1). Comment on the owning row and `moe.report_blocked` — do not patch across the seam.
